item.title: 如果你折磨数字足够长的时间，它们会告诉你任何你想听的事情。也就是说，一项指标表明
item.description:
如果你折磨数字足够长的时间，它们会告诉你任何你想听的事情。也就是说，一项指标表明半决赛可能已经创出相对低点，或者下一轮下跌可能是它们开始相对表现优于之前的最后一段。
超卖反弹可能是爆炸性的，并且可以持续足够长的时间以实现有利可图的交易。它们不是我交易的类型，但对于那些愿意交易波动性的人来说肯定有机会。
对于那些指出显而易见的事实的人来说——半决赛最终将上演一场强大的反弹——在某些时候你会是对的。问题不在于遭受重挫的股票是否会反弹。问题是你是否能够确定反弹何时发生，管理与回报相关的风险，以及反弹是否足够可持续以赚钱。

If you torture numbers long enough, they’ll tell you anything you want to hear. That said, one indicator suggests that semis may have already made a relative low - or that the next leg down could be the last before they begin outperforming on a relative basis.
Oversold rallies can be explosive and can last long enough to trade profitably. They’re not the type of setups I trade, but there could certainly be opportunity for those willing to trade the volatility.
And to those pointing out the obvious - that semis will eventually stage a powerful rally - you’ll be right at some point. The question isn’t whether beaten-down stocks will rally. The question is whether you can identify when the rally will occur, manage risk in relation to reward, and if the rally is sustainable enough to make money doing it.

item.title: $SPCX 以教科书式的方式发挥作用。正如我三个月前建议的那样。
item.description:
$SPCX 以教科书式的方式发挥作用。正如我三个月前建议的那样。

$SPCX playing out in textbook fashion. As I suggested three months ago.

@markminervini

开销供应快速恢复的概念可能正在 $SPCX 中体现。它开始看起来与 Facebook 类似。时间会证明一切。

LinkedIn 是另一个很好的例子。 2011年上市后，该股经历了连续六周的大幅下跌，随后强势反弹，几乎一路回到历史高点。但它很快就被管理费用所淹没。

我直到 2013 年第一季度才开始购买 LinkedIn。这就是该股票吸收供应、建立适当结构并最终启动重大举措所需的时间。

一个好的设置需要时间来开发。您想要的不是最低的价格...您想要的是合适的价格。正确的价格是指股票几乎立即进入强劲价格走势而不会触及止损的点。

The concept of a quick recovery running into overhead supply may be playing out in $SPCX. It’s starting to look similar to the Facebook analog. Time will tell.

LinkedIn was another great example. After going public in 2011, the stock suffered a huge six-week decline, then staged a powerful recovery almost all the way back to its old high. But it quickly became overwhelmed by overhead supply.

I didn’t start buying LinkedIn until the first quarter of 2013. That’s how long it took for the stock to absorb the supply, build a proper structure, and finally launch into a major move.

A great setup takes time to develop. You don't want the lowest price... you want the right price. The right price is the point at which the stock moves up into a strong price move almost immediately without hitting your stop-loss.

item.title: 这正是信息被误解然后被黑客纸上谈兵的专家滥用的方式。 这个👇博客“研究”完全具有误
item.description:
这正是信息被误解然后被黑客纸上谈兵的专家滥用的方式。
这个👇博客“研究”完全具有误导性，因为它始于错误的假设。趋势模板不是交易策略，而是限定符。它的目的从来不是为了告诉你买什么、何时买、在哪里卖或如何管理风险。这只是我在应用其余标准之前用来确定股票资格的工具之一。
测试趋势模板就好像它是一个完整的策略一样，就像要求锤子建造房屋，或者要求赛车底盘赢得比赛一样。
趋势模板是趋势跟踪策略的必要工具，但它只是众多工具之一。
这就是为什么在股市中表现出色的人很少。他们在灰质世界中寻找黑白答案和神奇公式。

This is exactly how information gets misunderstood and then misused by hack armchair pundits.
This 👇blog "study" is totally misleading because it starts with the wrong assumption. The Trend Template is not a trading strategy, it’s a qualifier. It was never designed to tell you what to buy, when to buy, where to sell, or how to manage risk. It’s simply one of the tools I use to qualify stocks before applying the rest of my criteria.
Testing the Trend Template as though it were a complete strategy is like asking a hammer to build a house, or asking a race car chassis to win a race.
The Trend Template is a necessary tool for a trend following strategy, but it’s only one of many.
This is why so few do well in the stock market; they're looking for black & white answers and magical formulas in a world of grey matter.

@sack

.@markminervini 的趋势模板是复制最多的库存屏幕之一。

自 1995 年以来，我每个月都会对 30 只美国大型股票进行分析。一只股票通过后的一个月，其回报率为 +1.61%。失败后，+1.55%。自2020年以来，通过是最糟糕的迹象。

https://www.edgeandnoise.com/p/mark-minervini-trend-template-backtest

.@markminervini's Trend Template is one of the most copied stock screens.

I ran it on 30 large US stocks, every month since 1995. The month after a stock passed, it returned +1.61%. After a fail, +1.55%. Since 2020, passing was the worse sign.

https://www.edgeandnoise.com/p/mark-minervini-trend-template-backtest

item.title: 任何以他的自杀为理由不将杰西·利弗莫尔列入最伟大交易者名单的人都完全不知道他是谁
item.description:
任何以他的自杀为理由不将杰西·利弗莫尔列入最伟大交易者名单的人都完全不知道他是谁以及他取得了什么成就。我会把杰西列为第一。
1929 年，杰西·利弗莫尔 (Jesse Livermore) 通过做空市场赚了 1 亿美元，相当于今天的近 20 亿美元。
正确看待这一点：卖空的最大可能收益是 100%。利弗莫尔并不是偶然发现亚马逊并持有它二十年的。他通过阅读市场并在大额赌注上选择空头时机而获得了这笔财富。毫无疑问🐐

Anyone who uses his suicide as a reason not to put Jesse Livermore on the list of greatest traders is completely ignorant to who he was and what he accomplished. I would rank Jesse number one.
Jesse Livermore made $100 million shorting the market in 1929 -nearly $2 billion in today’s dollars.
Put that in perspective: the maximum possible gain on a short sale is 100%. Livermore didn’t stumble onto Amazon and hold it for two decades. He made that fortune by reading the market and timing his shorts on massive bets. Without a doubt the 🐐

With all do respect, any list that doesn't include Jesse Livermore and Bill O'Neil is incomplete.
